text: You're online, adding items to your cart. Life intervenes. You close the tab, expecting your selections to vanish.
Hours later, you return. Open the site, certain your cart is gone. But there it is: full, as you left it. Magical, right?
Is it your browser remembering? A bookmark? You might think items wait inside your computer. But that's not the whole truth.
Adding an item assigns a unique ID, a cookie. This links your cart to *their* server database. Your browser sends that ID to pull up your saved cart.
This isn't just kindness. It's strategic. Saving your cart removes friction, making purchase easier. They're recovering lost sales.
Next time your cart waits, remember: it's not magic. It's a clever system guiding you back to checkout. Convenient, yes, but a quiet nudge.
